days.title: Kuala Lumpur to Ho Chi Minh
days.note: Have the Visit Japan Web QR codes screenshotted before you board. Airport wifi is not a plan.

items.title: Lunch
items.desc: Kyochon 1991

items.title: At KLIA Terminal 1
items.desc: Check in for VN678. One checked bag each.

items.title: Snack at Coffee Bean
items.desc: Eat before boarding. The transit is late at night.

items.title: VN678 departs
items.desc: Lands at Tan Son Nhat Terminal 2 at 20:55.

items.title: Transit, 3 hours 10 minutes
items.desc: Stay airside. No Vietnam transit visa is needed because neither leg flies between two Vietnamese cities. Snack, then sleep on VN320.

items.title: VN320 to Osaka
items.desc: Overnight to Kansai, arriving 07:00.

items.title: Buy
items.desc:
Cigarette - $3
2x Neck Pillow - $16
Mint - $3

days.title: Land in Osaka
days.note: Cap today at about 12,000 steps and be in bed by 22:30. Treating the red-eye arrival as a full sightseeing day is the classic way to wreck a Japan trip.

items.title: To Namba, drop the bags
items.desc: Nankai Airport Express, 45 minutes, ¥970. Leave the bags at Fourz Hotel Kintetsu Osaka Namba (check-in is 15:00).

items.title: Easy walk
items.desc: Shinsaibashi arcade, then Kuromon Ichiba Market for a few bites, or Shinsekai and Tsutenkaku. Keep it slow.

items.title: Check in and sleep
items.desc: Ninety minutes. You will have been awake about 30 hours and this nap is what makes Days 2 and 3 work.

items.title: Dotonbori
items.desc: Glico sign, Ebisu bridge, Hozenji Yokocho lanterns. Do not queue longer than 20 minutes for anything tonight.

items.title: Buy
items.desc: Alcohol

days.title: Osaka at an easy pace
days.note: The morning is free now that Osaka Castle is out. Nara still fits if you want it: Kintetsu Nara line direct from Osaka Namba, 40 minutes, ¥680. Leave 07:30, deer and Todai-ji by 09:00, back by 14:00 for Umeda at sunset.

items.title: Breakfast near Namba
items.desc: Slow start.

items.title: Umeda browsing
items.desc: Hankyu and Daimaru department stores, Grand Front, the HEP Five Ferris wheel.

items.title: Umeda Sky Building
items.desc: Floating Garden Observatory, about ¥2,000. The 16:00 slot gets daylight, the 16:47 sunset and the night skyline on one ticket.

days.title: Move to Kyoto
days.note: Sunday 22 and Monday 23 are the Sunday and public holiday of a three-day weekend landing on peak foliage. These are the two hardest days of the trip.

items.title: Leave Namba
items.desc: Midosuji subway to Umeda, then the JR Special Rapid. About 50 minutes and ¥820 all in. Kyoto Station by 08:30.

items.title: Bags first
items.desc: Hotel early drop, or a Kyoto Station coin locker. Lockers are full by 10:00 this season, so do this before anything else.

items.title: Fushimi Inari
items.desc: Two stops on the JR Nara line, free and always open. Walk past the busy lower gates up to the Yotsutsuji viewpoint, about 45 minutes. Most visitors turn back well before that.

items.title: Lunch near Fushimi Inari
items.desc: Kitsune udon or inari sushi around the shrine.

items.title: Nishiki Market
items.desc: Then the Teramachi arcades. Covered and crowd tolerant, which is what you want on a holiday Sunday.

items.title: Hotel, rest
items.desc: Do not skip this one.

items.title: Eikan-do lit up
items.desc: Night illumination runs about 17:30 to 21:00, ¥600 to ¥700. Arrive around 19:30 rather than at opening; the first wave clears and the queue collapses.

days.title: Kiyomizu at dawn, Sagano train
days.note: Public holiday. Arashiyama will be busy by mid-morning, so use the Tenryu-ji north gate straight into the bamboo grove and keep moving. Avoid Kyoto city buses all day: subway, JR and taxis only.

items.title: Kiyomizu-dera
items.desc: Opens 06:00. At the gate by 06:15 you share the wooden stage with about thirty people instead of two thousand. Walk down Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka at 07:15 while they are still empty.

items.title: Coffee and breakfast in Higashiyama
items.desc: Around Ninenzaka or a konbini on the way down.

items.title: Yasaka Shrine and Maruyama Park
items.desc: Short loop, still quiet at this hour.

items.title: To Arashiyama
items.desc: To Kyoto Station, then the JR Sagano line to Saga-Arashiyama, 15 minutes. Allow about 45 minutes door to door. A taxi is fine for two if the timing slips.

items.title: Tenryu-ji and the bamboo grove
items.desc: Garden about ¥500. The Sogenchi pond against the autumn hillside, then out the north gate into the bamboo grove. Togetsukyo bridge after.

items.title: Lunch in Arashiyama
items.desc: Yudofu (simmered tofu) or soba. Eat by 12:30 so you are not rushing for the train.

items.title: Sagano Romantic Train
items.desc: Be at Torokko Saga station (next to JR Saga-Arashiyama) by 13:30 with your tickets ready. About 25 minutes along the Hozu gorge to Torokko Kameoka. Walk about 10 minutes to JR Umahori and ride the Sagano line back to Kyoto.

items.title: Back in Kyoto, rest
items.desc: Early night. Tomorrow you check out and move to Tokyo.

items.title: Dinner at Kyoto Station
items.desc: Ramen Koji on the 10th floor, or Kyoto Tower.

days.title: Uji, then the bullet train
days.note: Reserve the 16:30 Shinkansen ahead (Smart EX). Sunset is around 16:30, so Mount Fuji will be dark by the time you pass it.

items.title: Breakfast near the hotel
items.desc: Check out, leave the bags at the hotel or in a Kyoto Station locker.

items.title: To Uji
items.desc: JR Nara line from Kyoto Station, about 20 to 30 minutes, ¥240.

items.title: Byodo-in Phoenix Hall
items.desc: Opens 08:30, about ¥700. The interior tour of the Phoenix Hall is a separate timed ticket sold on site, so buy it first.

items.title: Byodoin Omotesando and the river
items.desc: Matcha houses along the approach, the Uji bridge, Ujigami Shrine across the river.

items.title: Matcha lunch in Uji
items.desc: Matcha soba and a parfait. Ahead of the noon rush.

items.title: Back to Kyoto, collect bags
items.desc: Last browse at Kyoto Station (Porta, Isetan). Buy an ekiben for the train.

items.title: Shinkansen to Tokyo
items.desc: About 2 hours 15 minutes on a Nozomi. Then the Yamanote or Keihin-Tohoku line to Ueno, eight minutes. Check in at Four Points Flex by Sheraton Tokyo Ueno.

items.title: Dinner at Ameyoko
items.desc: Market under the tracks, five minutes from the hotel. Easy first Tokyo evening.

days.title: Mount Fuji, Rikugien at night
days.note: Lake-level colour usually peaks in early November, so the maples may be past their best. What you gain is a snow-capped Fuji and clearer winter air. Book the return bus before the outbound one.

items.title: Decide the night before
items.desc: Check the Fujigoko webcams and the forecast at 21:00 on the 24th. Clear morning, go. Thick cloud, swap this day with Saturday and do Tokyo instead.

items.title: Konbini breakfast
items.desc: Eat on the way or at Busta Shinjuku.

items.title: Leave Ueno for Busta Shinjuku
items.desc: The 07:25 highway bus reaches Kawaguchiko about 09:10 and is the last slot before expressway traffic builds. About ¥2,200 each way.

items.title: Oishi Park
items.desc: Buy the Fuji Five Lakes bus pass, about ¥1,700, then the Red Line to the north shore. Fuji holds its shape through the morning and hides in cloud after that, so go here first.

items.title: Kawaguchiko Ropeway
items.desc: To Tenjoyama, about ¥1,000 return.

items.title: Hoto for lunch
items.desc: The local hand-cut udon in miso broth.

items.title: Pick one
items.desc: Maple Corridor by the lake, or the Fujikyu line to Shimo-Yoshida and 398 steps up to Chureito Pagoda. One, not both.

items.title: Return bus to Shinjuku
items.desc: Arrives Shinjuku about 17:15 to 18:15 depending on traffic.

items.title: Rikugien evening illumination
items.desc: JR Yamanote line from Shinjuku to Komagome, about 20 minutes, then 7 minutes on foot to the Somei gate. Lit-up maples around the pond. About ¥300, open to around 21:00 with last entry around 20:30. Check this year's dates before you go.

items.title: Dinner near Komagome or Ueno
items.desc: Komagome to Ueno is about 10 minutes on the Yamanote line.

days.title: Tokyo DisneySea
days.note: Have the app installed, logged in and both tickets linked before you arrive. Fantasy Springs runs entirely through the app and is issued within minutes of opening.

items.title: Leave Ueno
items.desc: To Tokyo Station, JR Keiyo line to Maihama, then the Disney Resort Line. Allow 20 minutes inside Tokyo Station alone; the Keiyo platforms are a long underground walk. At the gate by 08:15 for a 09:00 opening.

items.title: Ride order
items.desc: Soaring: Fantastic Flight, Journey to the Center of the Earth, Tower of Terror, Indiana Jones, Toy Story Mania, then Fantasy Springs. Venetian Gondolas once at dusk.

items.title: Lunch in the park
items.desc: Mobile order in the app to skip the queue.

items.title: Dinner in the park
items.desc: Before you claim a spot for the night show.

items.title: Hold a harbour spot
items.desc: Take a position about 40 minutes before the night show. Mediterranean Harbor is the best viewing bowl in any Disney park.

items.title: To Kawasaki
items.desc: JR to Shinjuku, Odakyu line to Noborito about 18 minutes, then the shuttle bus, ¥220 and ten minutes. About 70 minutes door to door. Noborito is itself a Doraemon-themed station.

items.title: Fujiko F. Fujio Museum
items.desc: Your 10:00 slot, about ¥1,000. Timed and advance only. Allow two and a half hours. The rooftop has the Anywhere Door, Pisuke's pond and the concrete pipes in the vacant lot. Themed cafe and a shop with goods sold nowhere else.

items.title: Lunch at the museum cafe or in Shinjuku
Shinjuku Gyoen
items.desc: ¥500, last entry about 15:30. Late November is when the ginkgo avenue and the maples peak here.

items.title: Shibuya Sky
items.desc: Scramble crossing first, then your booked slot, about ¥3,000. 16:00 gets daylight, the 16:30 sunset and the lit city on one ticket.

items.title: Dinner in Shibuya or Harajuku
items.desc: Or Omoide Yokocho back in Shinjuku for grilled skewers in a lane of tiny bars.

days.title: Old Tokyo and the shopping run
days.note: Deliberately central and low commitment so it can absorb a swap if Fuji has to move. Reserve the Skyliner for tomorrow morning today.

items.title: Asakusa
items.desc: Senso-ji and the Kaminarimon gate. Nakamise is deserted before 08:30 and unwalkable by 11:00. Photograph first, shop later.

items.title: Skytree and Solamachi
items.desc: Walk up Sumida Park. Solamachi opens 10:00 and has the Doraemon Mirai Department Store, no ticket needed. The Tembo Deck is optional at about ¥2,400.

items.title: One district only
items.desc: Akihabara, Ginza, or Tokyo Station Character Street. Saturday crowds mean one, not three.

items.title: Ueno shopping run
items.desc: Ginkgo avenue in the park, then Ameyoko, Don Quijote and a drugstore sweep. Every receipt goes in one envelope for the airport tax refund.

items.title: Pack properly
items.desc: Weigh both bags, lay out tomorrow's clothes and passports, set two alarms. You are up at 04:45.

days.title: Narita and home
days.note: If the tax refund queue looks longer than an hour, walk away and check in. The flight is worth far more than the tax.

items.title: Up
items.desc: Final sweep of the room: safe, bathroom, charger, under the bed.

items.title: Skyliner to Narita
items.desc: Walk to Keisei Ueno. First Skyliner is around 05:40 to 06:00 and reaches Terminal 1 in about 45 minutes, roughly ¥2,580 each. Confirm the Sunday first departure when you reserve.

items.title: Tax refund
items.desc: Before you check bags; customs may want to see the goods. Passport, boarding pass, receipts, unopened items. Allow 45 to 60 minutes.

items.title: Breakfast at Narita
items.desc: After check-in, airside.

items.title: Check in
items.desc: Vietnam Airlines, Terminal 1. Confirm bags are tagged through to Kuala Lumpur and mention the 60 minute connection at Hanoi.

items.title: VN311
items.desc: Hanoi at 13:50, then VN681 at 14:50 into Kuala Lumpur at 19:10. Move briskly at Noi Bai and do not shop.
